K5AX: Bani of Guru Nanak Dev ji in Raag Vadhans, Ghar 5: 'Alahnian'.
Raag Wadahans, First Mehl, Fifth House, Alaahanees ~ Songs Of Mourning:
Alahnian⁽¹⁾ is the name for weeping while telling the virtues of those who have died — that is, words full of detachment are uttered.
AANY: Akal Purakh is one, and is met by the Satguru's grace.
One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:
There is but One God. By True Guru's grace He is obtained.
Y4JW: Dhan = worthy of praise. Siranda = the one who creates, the Creator. Sacha = ever-abiding. Jin = who (the King). Dhandhai = in the pursuits (of Maya).
That Creator-King is ever-abiding, who has set the world to the pursuits of Maya.
Blessed is the Creator, the True King, who has linked the whole world to its tasks.
Blessed is the Creator, the True king, who has engages the world in its tasks.
Blessed is the true King, Akal Purakh, the (siranda) maker of the world, who has set the whole world to its occupations.
8Y24: Muhlat = the time given. Puni = is reached, is completed. Pai = the cup of the water-clock. Janiarha = the beloved companion, the soul. Ghat = seizing. Chalaia = is driven on ahead.
When the time given to a being runs out, and the cup of its lifespan fills, then the beloved companion (of the body) is seized and driven on ahead.
When one's time is up, and the measure is full, this dear soul is caught, and driven off.
when the time is over and the measure is full, this dear soul is caught and driven off.

When the (muhlat) span of life ran out — like a filled (pai) measuring bowl; that is, just as when a measure for grain is filled and turned over, no grain stays in it, so when the breath no longer stays — then the (janiarha) beloved soul is seized, a chain is (ghat) put around its neck, and it is driven on the road of Yama; the meaning is, the messengers of Yama led it away.

LLUF: Chalaia = is driven on ahead. Veer sabae = all the brothers, all friends and relatives.
(When life's time is over) and Parmatma's written (order) comes, all friends and relatives weep.
This dear soul is driven off, when the pre-ordained Order is received, and all the relatives cry out in mourning.
When the writ is received, the dear soul is driven off and all the brethren bewail.
When what was written came, and the soul was chained and (chalaia) led away, then all the (bir) brothers there were, (sabae) all of them, wept.
EX72: Hans = the soul. Punne = run out, ended. Mae = O mother!
O my mother! When the days of life are complete, body and soul are separated (forever).
The body and the swan-soul are separated, when one's days are past and done, O my mother.
When mortal's days are at an end, the body and the swan soul are separated, O my mother.
So, O my (mae) sister! When the days were complete, the (hans) soul was separated from the body.
7B8Y: Purab = in the time before death.
According to the deeds a being has earned beforehand (before that final moment), such is the destiny of impressions written (on its forehead), and such is the fruit the being receives.
As is one's pre-ordained Destiny, so does one receive, according to one's past actions.
As is the writ and as are his former acts, so obtains he.
As was written before, so the fruit has been received now; and as one earns now, so will the fruit be hereafter.
1LGJ: That Creator-King is ever-abiding, who has set the world to the pursuits of Maya. ||1||
Blessed is the Creator, the True King, who has linked the whole world to its tasks. ||1||
Hail to the Creator, the True King, who has engaged the world in its task.
Blessed is the true King, Parmeshvar, the maker, who created the world and set it to its dealings. ||1||
EB6Z: O my brothers! Remember the (ever-abiding) Master, the Prabhu. Everyone must make this departure (from the world).
Meditate in remembrance on the Lord and Master, O my Siblings of Destiny; everyone has to pass this way.
Remember the Lord, O my brethren. All have to go this way.
O my brothers! Everyone will have to (paiana) go from this world in the same way, so remember the Master.
ZH7Z: Ethai = in this world. Sarpar = surely.
The false pursuit of Maya in the world lasts only four days; (everyone) must surely go on from here (to the world beyond).
These false entanglements last for only a few days; then, one must surely move on to the world hereafter.
The false strife here is only for four (a few) days and then one assuredly proceeds onwards.
(Ethai) In this world the false business lasts four days; hereafter, in the next world, one must (sarpar) certainly go.
W42D: (Everyone) must surely go on from here; (here in the world) we are like guests; to take pride (in any wealth or possessions) is useless.
He must surely move on to the world hereafter, like a guest; so why does he indulge in ego?
For sure, one proceeds into the Yond like a guest. Why should then one indulge in ego?
One must certainly go hereafter to the next world, and in the world the soul is like a (mihmana) guest — so why should we be proud?
SKA9: We should remember the Name of that Parmatma alone, by remembering whom spiritual bliss is found in Parmatma's presence.
Chant the Name of the Lord; serving Him, you shall obtain peace in His Court.
Repeat the Name of Him, by serving whom, you shall obtain peace in His court.
Let us remember the Name of that very Akal Purakh, by whose service we find peace in the Court.
WPQU: Moole = at all. Sir sir = on each one's head. Kia = what was done, each one's own deeds. Vihana = passes, befalls.
In the world beyond no one's command can prevail at all; there, what befalls each one's head follows what (each has) done.
In the world hereafter, no one's commands will be obeyed. According to their actions, each and every person proceeds.
In the next world, in no wise can man's command run every one fares according to his acts.

Hereafter, in the realm of Yama, no command prevails (moole) at all; what befalls each head — that is, all beings — (vihana) passes according to the deeds they did; the meaning is, one must undergo the fruit of one's deeds.
WYGM: O my brothers! Remember the (ever-abiding) Master, the Prabhu. Everyone must make this departure (from the world). ||2||
Meditate in remembrance on the Lord and Master, O my Siblings of Destiny; everyone has to pass this way. ||2||
Meditate on the Lord, O my brethren, for all shall have to go this way.
All beings will make their (paiana) departure — that is, will die — from this world, so, O my brother, remember the Master. ||2||
DP0J: Samrath = all-powerful. Hilarha = a pretext. Sansaro = (meaning) the efforts of worldly beings.
The efforts of the world's beings are only a pretext; what happens is whatever pleases that all-powerful Prabhu.
Whatever pleases the Almighty Lord, that alone comes to pass; this world is an opportunity to please Him.
Whatever pleases the Omnipotent Lord, that alone comes to pass. This world is an opportunity to earn His pleasure.
This world is (hilarha) full of suffering; in it, whatever pleases the all-powerful Akal Purakh, that alone (thiai) happens.
THBT: Mahial = mahi tal, on the surface of the earth, in the space above the earth, in the sky.
That ever-abiding Creator is present everywhere — in water, on land, in the sky.
The True Creator Lord is pervading and permeating the water, the land and the air.
The True Creator is pervading the ocean, the earth, the nether regions and the firmament.
That true Creator is pervading everything — the underworld, the earth, the sky.
L5RL: That Prabhu is ever-abiding, the maker of all, unseen, boundless; no being can find the end of His virtues.
The True Creator Lord is invisible and infinite; His limits cannot be found.
The True Creator is invisible and infinite. His limit cannot be determined.
That true, unseen, boundless One is the maker of the world; no one has found His end.
DLB3: Ik man = with one mind, with attention joined.
Only the birth of those in the world is called fruitful who have remembered that boundless Prabhu with attention joined.
Fruitful is the coming of those, who meditate single-mindedly on Him.
Fruitful is the advent of those who, singly-mindedly, contemplate over the Lord.
Those who have meditated on that boundless Akal Purakh — their coming into the world has been fruitful.
D4HV: Dhah = having torn down. Hukam = by His command.
Parmatma Himself tears down the created world, and having torn it down He Himself builds it again; by His command He makes beings live good lives.
He destroys, and having destroyed, He creates; by His Order, He adorns us.
The Adorner, by His command demolishes and having demolished, Himself constructs.
He Himself, by His command, (dhah) destroys; then Himself, having destroyed, (savare) brings forth again.
K15G: The efforts of the world's beings are only a pretext; what happens is whatever seems good to that all-powerful Prabhu. ||3||
Whatever pleases the Almighty Lord, that alone comes to pass; this world is an opportunity to please Him. ||3||
Whatever pleases the All-powerful Lord, that happens. This world is an opportunity to earn His pleasure.
Whatever pleases that all-powerful One happens; this world is full of suffering. ||3||
U0FX: Baba = O brother! Runna janiai = take it that one has truly come to detachment.
O Nanak! Know that person alone to have truly come to detachment who comes to detachment with love (for the sake of union with Parmatma).
Nanak: he alone truly weeps, O Baba, who weeps in the Lord's Love.
Says Nanak, O father, one is deemed to weep truly, if weeps in the Lord's love.
Sri Guru ji says: (baba) O brother! Know that person's weeping as weeping, who weeps with love attached.
MGAS: Valeve karan = for the sake of wealth and possessions. Bikaro = useless, in vain.
O brother! The weeping one does for the sake of the world's wealth and possessions all goes to waste.
One who weeps for the sake of worldly objects, O Baba, weeps totally in vain.
O father, the mortal bewails for the sake of worldly objects, therefore, all his bewailing is in vain.
And the weeping of worldly people is for the sake of (valeve) things, and such weeping is all a form of vice.
U7CD: Bikaro = useless, in vain. Gafal = heedless, careless.
The world, having forgotten Parmatma, weeps for the sake of Maya; all this weeping is in vain.
This weeping is all in vain; the world forgets the Lord, and weeps for the sake of Maya.
All the weeping is in vain. The world is forgetful of the Lord and weeps for wealth.
All the weeping is vice — that is, in vain; this whole world, (gafal) having forgotten, weeps for the sake of Maya.
W3CS: A person cannot recognise good deeds from bad; (weeping and weeping for Maya) he destroys this body in vain.
He does not distinguish between good and evil, and wastes away this life in vain.
Between good and evil, the mortal does not make any discrimination and wastes away this life in vain.
He understands nothing of good and bad, and wastes this body for nothing.
FD3M: Koorh = for the sake of the perishable world.
Whoever has come into the world (by being born) will go (when his time is over); caught in attachment to the perishable world, you take (useless) pride.
Everyone who comes here, shall have to leave; to act in ego is false.
All those who come here shall go Hence false it is to act in pride.
Whoever has come into this world by birth will surely go by death; so you take false pride in the world.
EAF4: Baba = O brother! Runna janiai = take it that one has truly come to detachment. ||4||1||
O Nanak! Know that person alone to have truly come to detachment who comes to detachment with love (for the sake of union with Parmatma). ||4||1||
Nanak: he alone truly weeps, O Baba, who weeps in the Lord's Love. ||4||1||
Says Nanak, O father, a man is considered to wail truly, if he wails in the Lord's love.
Sri Guru ji says: O brother! Know weeping to be fruitful only when the soul weeps with love attached to Parmeshvar; the meaning is, when there is detachment. ||4||1||
FKVY: Laehan = let us take. Sacharha = ever-abiding.
O companions! (O friends of the sat sangat!) Come, let us sit together and remember Parmatma's ever-abiding Name.
Come, O my companions - let us meet together and dwell upon the True Name.
Come mates, let us meet and contemplate over the True Name.
O companions! Come, meet, let us remember the true Name together.
APNR: Rovah = let us weep, let us grieve. Birha = separation. Tan = body.
Come, let us recall again and again, with sorrow, our separation from the Prabhu; (to end that separation) let us remember the Master, the Prabhu.
Let us weep over the body's separation from the Lord and Master; let us remember Him in contemplation.
Let us bewail over our body's (soul's) separation from the Lord and remember Him.
Let us remember our own Master, and weep in memory of the separation from Hari's body — that is, His true form.
SSZJ: Samhalih = let us remember. Panth = road. Nihalih = let us look.
Come, let us enshrine the Master in the heart, and look at that road (on which all are going). We too must go (in the end) to that world beyond (where countless have gone already).
Let us remember the Lord and Master in contemplation, and keep a watchful eye on the Path. We shall have to go there as well.
Let us cherish the Lord and keep an eye on the Path, We, too have to go there.
Remember the Master, and let us look at the road by which beings went before; we too must go by it.
939T: Kia = created. Lia = took back. Bhana = will.
(Weeping at anyone's death is useless.) The Prabhu who had created this one has taken the life back; it is His will that has come about.
He who has created, also destroys; whatever happens is by His Will.
He, who created, also destroys All that taken place is in His will.
The One by whom this soul was made has taken it by death, and what was His will has come about.
893H: Whatever a being has done here in the world comes before him (at death). (Before this divine law) we have no power at all.
Whatever He has done, has come to pass; how can we command Him?
Whatever He has done, that has happened. How can we give the command?
The deeds he did before came before him — that is, he had to undergo them. What command can we give — that is, we cannot say, 'Why did You give suffering? Give happiness.'
HSEA: O companions! (O friends of the sat sangat!) Come, let us sit together and remember the Name of the ever-abiding Prabhu. ||1||
Come, O my companions - let us meet together and dwell upon the True Name. ||1||
Come and meet me, O maids; let us take the True Name.
O dear ones! Come, meet, and together let us take — that is, repeat — the true Name. ||1||
GQHT: Loka = O people! Aisa = such a death.
O people! Do not call death bad (death is good — but only) if a person knows how to die in that way (having lived rightly).
Death would not be called bad, O people, if one knew how to truly die.
O people, let us not call death bad. There is hardly any such person, Who knows how to die.
O people! If someone knows how to die in this way, then one should not say that death is bad.
Q9XK: Samrath = with all powers. Suhela = easy.
(That way is this:) remember your all-powerful Master, (so that on the journey of life) the road becomes easy.
Serve your Almighty Lord and Master, and your path in the world hereafter will be easy.
Serve, you your Omnipotent Lord. Thus, your path in the Yond shall be easy to tread.
Serve your all-powerful Master, so that the road ahead to the next world becomes (suhela) easy.
SF0Q: Panth suhelai = on the easy road. Aagai = in the Prabhu's presence. Vadai = honour.
(By the blessing of remembrance) if you walk the easy road of life, you will receive its fruit too, and honour in the Prabhu's presence.
Take this easy path, and you shall obtain the fruits of your rewards, and receive honor in the world hereafter.
If you go by the easy route, then shall you gather fruit and receive honour in the world beyond.
Only if you go by the easy road will you receive the fruit that is peace, and hereafter you will receive greatness too.
EE7E: Bhetai siu = taking the offering (of the Name). Sach = in the ever-abiding Prabhu. Lekhai = when the account of deeds is taken.
If you go taking the offering of the Prabhu's Name, you will become one with that ever-abiding Prabhu, and when the account of deeds is taken you will receive honour.
Go there with your offering, and you shall merge in the True Lord; your honor shall be confirmed.
If you go with the offering of meditation then shall you merge in the True Lord and your honour will be approved.
If you go taking the (bhetai siu) offering of the remembrance of the Name with you, then you will merge into peace, and only then will your honour be counted in the reckoning.
CLZ3: Mahli = in the presence. Rang siu = with love.
You will find a place in the Prabhu's presence and be pleasing to the Master, the Prabhu, and so, with love for the Prabhu, you will enjoy spiritual bliss.
You shall obtain a place in the Mansion of the Lord Master's Presence; being pleasing to Him, you shall enjoy the pleasures of His Love.
You shall obtain place in the Master's mansion be pleasing to Him and enjoy revelments with love.
In this way you will please the Master, then find a place in the palaces, and enjoy delights with joy.
WCSL: O people! Do not call death bad (but only that one understands this) who knows how to die in this way. ||2||
Death would not be called bad, O people, if one knew how to truly die. ||2||
if one knows how to die, O people then, death would not be called bad.
O people! Death is not to be called bad — if someone knows how to die; the meaning is, gives up the sense of being a separate self. ||2||
3QUY: Hak = rightful, accepted. Jo = those who.
The people who die accepted (in the Prabhu's eyes, while still living) are heroes; their death too is praised (in this world and the next).
The death of brave heroes is blessed, if it is approved by God.
Fruitful is the dying of the brave persons, whose death is approved by the Lord. (die for a good cause).
The death of those heroic men is (hak) true who die having been accepted — or who, having died, are accepted.

SWX6: In the Prabhu's presence only those people are called heroes; they receive honour in the court of the ever-abiding Prabhu.
They alone are acclaimed as brave warriors in the world hereafter, who receive true honor in the Court of the Lord.
Hereafter, they alone are acclaimed as warriors, who receive true honour in the Lord's court.
And they alone are called heroes who receive honour in the true Court hereafter.
CSNJ: They receive honour in the Court, they go (from here) with honour, and in the world beyond no suffering touches them.
They are honored in the Court of the Lord; they depart with honor, and they do not suffer pain in the world hereafter.
They depart with honour, obtain glory in the Lord's court and suffer not pain in the next world.
They receive honour in the next world, they go with dignity, and hereafter no suffering of any kind touches them.
CCJD: Those people remember Parmatma, knowing Him to be present (everywhere); they receive the fruit from the door of that Prabhu, by remembering whom (every kind of) fear goes away.
They meditate on the One Lord, and obtain the fruits of their rewards. Serving the Lord, their fear is dispelled.
Deeming the Lord but One, they dwell upon Him and then gather reward. The Lord is such, by serving whom, the fear is dispelled.
They meditate on the one Akal Purakh; only then do they receive the fruit of human birth. What is Hari like? The One by whose service all fears run away.
JN55: Ooncha = a proud word. Jano = the knowing Prabhu.
One should not speak a word of pride; one should keep oneself under control. That Prabhu, the knower of hearts, Himself knows every heart.
Do not indulge in egotism, and dwell within your own mind; the Knower Himself knows everything.
Indulge you not in ego and abide within yourself. The Knower Himself knows everything.
So, O brother, do not cry your sorrow out loud to anyone; rather, understanding it in the mind, one should stay silent, because that Knower Himself knows all good and bad.
TW1Y: Hak = rightful, accepted. Jo = those who. ||3||
The people who die accepted (in the Prabhu's eyes, while still living) are heroes; their death is praised (in this world and the next). ||3||
The death of brave heroes is blessed, if it is approved by God. ||3||
Profitable is the dying of the brave persons, whose death is approved by the Lord.
The death of those heroic men is true who, through worship, die fulfilled. ||3||
9SD3: O Nanak! This world is a play (the play keeps being set up and taken down); weeping at anyone's death is useless.
Nanak: for whom should we mourn, O Baba? This world is merely a play.
Says Nanak, whom should we wail for, a Sire, when this world is but a play?
Sri Guru ji says: O brother! For whom should we weep? This world is the show of a juggler — that is, it is not lasting.
HHBZ: Vekhai = takes care of. Kudrat = the created world.
The Master, the Prabhu, Himself takes care of the world He made; He Himself looks after the creation He made.
The Lord Master beholds His work, and contemplates His creative potency.
The Lord watches His craftsmanship and gives throughout to His creation.
The Master sees His own work alone, and reflects on it through His creative power.
3M59: The Prabhu keeps in mind the creation He made and gives it support and sustenance; the One who made the world also knows its needs.
He contemplates His creative potency, having established the Universe. He who created it, He alone knows.
He, who has created the universe, gives thought to His creation. He, who has created, alone knows.
Through His Maya He is holding up the world; and, having reflected on the good and bad deeds of beings, the One who made the world knows it.
BY7J: The Prabhu Himself sees the deeds everyone has done; He Himself understands every heart; He Himself recognises His own command (how this command is to be carried out in the world).
He Himself beholds it, and He Himself understands it. He Himself realizes the Hukam of His Command.
The Lord Himself sees, Himself understands and Himself realises He, His will.
God Himself sees; as a man of wisdom He understands; as a seeker He asks; as a devotee He recognises the command.
B6YE: The Prabhu who has made this created world knows its needs. That Prabhu's form is boundless.
He who created these things, He alone knows. His subtle form is infinite.
He who has made all this deal, alone knows it, Infinite is His beauty.
The One who made this whole world knows it, and that Hari's form is boundless.
LFKN: O Nanak! This world is a play (whatever is made here must break); weeping at anyone's death is useless. ||4||2||
Nanak: for whom should we mourn, O Baba? This world is merely a play. ||4||2||
Says Nanak, whom should we weep for, O father. This world is but a play.
Sri Guru ji says: O brother! For whom should we weep? This world is a play — that is, unreal. ||4||2||
8SS9: Sach = ever-abiding. Siranda = the Creator, the maker. Sacha = ever-abiding. Parvadgaro = the Sustainer.
Be sure that Parmatma, the maker of the world, alone is ever-abiding; that ever-abiding Prabhu is the sustainer (of beings),
The True Creator Lord is True - know this well; He is the True Sustainer.
Know the True Creator to be true. He is the True sustainer of all.
You are the true (siranda) Creator, the true (parvadgaro) Sustainer, and You are known as true.
W3Z3: Jin = who (the Creator). Aapinai = {aap hi nai} Himself. Aap = Himself. Alakh = unseen.
the Ever-abiding One who Himself made Himself manifest (in the form of the world); He is unseen and boundless.
He Himself fashioned His Own Self; the True Lord is invisible and infinite.
Invisible and Infinite is the True Lord, who Himself didst create His own being.
You, the true, unseen, boundless One, who from Yourself brought forth the world, Your own form.
BZG5: Dui purh = the two millstones (earth and sky). Vichhorhian = He has separated them, He has set them apart. Ghor andharo = pitch darkness.

Joining the two millstones (earth and sky) — that is, making the created world — that Prabhu has separated beings from Himself by catching them in attachment to Maya. Without the Guru there is pitch darkness (of attachment to Maya in the world).
He brought together, and then separated, the two grinding stones of the earth and the sky; without the Guru, there is only pitch darkness.
Creating the two mill-stones of the earth and the sky He has separated them. Without the Guru, there is pitch darkness.

Then You joined the two millstones, earth and sky — that is, created the universe — and then broke that sphere apart and made them separate. In that creation, without the Guru, there remains (ghor) very great darkness.
RBZW: Sirjian = He has made. Ah = day. Nis = night. Chalat = the (world-)play. ||1||
Parmatma Himself, making the sun and moon, has made this world-play of day and night. ||1||
He created the sun and the moon; night and day, they move according to His Thought. ||1||
The Lord created the sun and the moon. Realises that they are ever on the move.
And You made the sun and the moon, which keep moving night and day. ||1||
VJSG: (O Prabhu!) You are the Master who is ever-abiding. You Yourself give all beings the gift of love that lasts forever. ||Rahau||
O True Lord and Master, You are True. O True Lord, bless me with Your Love. ||Pause||
True You are, O True Lord. Bless me with Yours true affection. Pause.
Surely You are the true Master; so give me too Your true love. ||Rahau|| ☬ And what kind of true Master are You?
MMFL: (O Prabhu!) You alone created the world; You alone give (beings) sorrow and joy.
You created the Universe; You are the Giver of pain and pleasure.
You it is who created the world and you alone are the Giver of pain and pleasure.
You created the (medni) earth, and You alone are the giver of sorrows and joys.
UDN7: You created women and men too; You also made the attachment and love for the poison of Maya.
You created woman and man, the love of poison, and emotional attachment to Maya.
You have make woman and man as also the love of the poison of mammon and the temporal attachment.
You created women and men, and, through their attachment, there is love for Maya, which is poison.
GHYA: Khani = the four sources of creation (from eggs, from the womb, from sweat, from the earth). Bani = the languages of beings. Jia = to beings. Adharo = support.
The four sources of the birth of beings, and the languages of beings, are also made by You alone.
The four sources of creation, and the power of the Word, are also of Your making. You give Support to all beings.
The sources of creation and the power of speech are of Yours make and You givest them the true Support.
The four sources of life and the four forms of speech are all made by You alone; You alone give support to all beings.
B7UY: Sach = (joining beings) to the ever-abiding Name. Nibernharo = the one who decides, who settles the account. ||2||
(O Prabhu!) You alone give support to all beings. You alone have made this whole creation (as) a throne (to sit on); You Yourself settle the account of deeds too. ||2||
You have made the Creation as Your Throne; You are the True Judge. ||2||
The Creation, You has made Your throne and You alone are the true adjudicator.
You have (rachaia) made this throne of creation — Vaikunth, or the sat sangat, or the world, or the seat of Dharamraj — and You alone are the one who settles, who does true justice. ||2||
MMW9: Aavagavan = the round of birth and death. Thir = ever-abiding.
O Creator who does everything! You made the round of birth and death (for beings), but You Yourself are ever-abiding.
You created comings and goings, but You are ever-stable, O Creator Lord.
Coming and going You have ordained, but Yourself You are ever stable, O Creator.
You made the world of coming and going, and You alone are free of this coming and going, steady and unmoving — or You make beings unmoving; that is, You set them free.
55F9: Aai gaia = was born and died. Badhik = bound (in attachment). Jiu = the soul.
(Because of attachment to Maya) a being bound in vices is born and dies again and again; the round of birth and death keeps its hold on it.
In birth and death, in coming and going, this soul is held in bondage by corruption.
In birth and death, coming and going, this soul is bound in sins.
Birth and death have come upon this soul — or the soul has come into birth and death — and the vices are its (badhik) destroyer; or, through the vices, the soul has become violent.
4HFE: Bhoorhai = by the wretched one. Boorharai = of the one drowning. Charo = recourse, power.
The wretched being (caught in attachment to Maya) has forgotten (Your) Name; the one drowning in attachment gets nowhere.
The evil person has forgotten the Naam; he has drowned - what can he do now?
The evil person has forgotten the Name. The drowned one! What remedy has he, now?
The (bhoorhai) wretched being has forgotten the Name; what (charo) power does that (boorharai) drowning one have? That is, it has none.
DTPU: Giving up virtues, this being has gathered the poison (of vices); (coming into the world, all its life) it keeps trading in faults alone. ||3||
Forsaking merit, he has loaded the poisonous cargo of demerits; he is a trader of sins. ||3||
Forsaking merit, he, the trader of sin has loaded the poison of demerit.
The soul that is a trader in faults has given up the virtues and loaded itself with sins, which are poison. ||3||
7BU3: Jania = the soul (the body's companion). Hukam = by the command.
When, by the command of the ever-abiding Creator, the calls come for the soul to go from here,
The beloved soul has received the Call, the Command of the True Creator Lord.
By the True Creator's command, the beloved receives the call.
O true Creator! When, by Your command, the (sadrhe) summons came for those (jania) living beings — or those loved ones —
VTRA: then (at death) women and men are separated; and only Parmatma Himself is able to reunite the separated.
The soul, the husband, has become separated from the body, the bride. The Lord is the Re-uniter of the separated ones.
The soul spouse is separated from the body bride. Of the separated one, the Lord is the Uniter.
then women and men were separated from each other. Who then can reunite the separated? That is, no one — or, You alone are the one who reunites the separated.
2P4P: Sohniai = of the beautiful woman. Sir = on the head.
Yama cannot care about any beautiful woman's beauty (he grants no mercy from death), because he too is bound by Parmatma's command.
No one cares for your beauty, O beautiful bride.; the Messenger of Death is bound only by the Lord Commander's Command.
O Beauteous one, death cares not for beauty With the Commander's command the death's couriers are bound.
The work of the command is bound upon the heads of Yama's messengers, so they do not look at a form, (sohni) beautiful or not.
QND9: Yama's messengers care nothing for children or the old; in this way everyone's attachment and love (for one another) is broken. ||4||
He does not distinguish between young children and old people; he tears apart love and affection. ||4||
Between a child and an aged one, they (the yamas) distinguish not; they snap all love and affection.
He does not know the stage of child or old; his concern is in breaking the love there is. ||4||
7EQF: Nau dar = the nine doors, the nine openings (mouth, 2 ears, 2 nostrils, 2 eyes, anus, genital). Thake = were closed. Hans = the soul. Gainare = into the sky.
When by the command of the ever-abiding Parmatma the call comes for the soul to go, the nine doors (of the body) close, and the soul goes off (somewhere) into the sky.
The nine doors are closed by the True Lord's Command, and the swan-soul takes flight into the skies.
The nine doors are closed by the True Lord's order and the swan-soul goes out into the skies.
The nine doors, the nine openings, were all (thake) closed, and the (hans) soul set out on the road of the sky.
HUD2: Sa dhan = the wife, the body (the soul's wife). Chhuti = was left alone. Vidhania = {vi-dhani} without a husband. Mirtakrha = corpse. Anganrhe = in the courtyard.
(When the husband's soul departs,) the wife without a husband is left alone; robbed by attachment to Maya she has become a widow, and the corpse lies in the courtyard of the house.
The body-bride is separated, and defrauded by falsehood; she is now a widow - her husband's body lies dead in the courtyard.
The body bride is separated, defrauded by falsehood, she has become a widow and the dead body is lying at the door of, the compound.

(Sa dhan) that woman whose husband has died is (chhuti) left without her husband. Sri Guru ji says: she who was enchanted by the false world says, "I have been (muthi) robbed." She is (vidhania) grief-stricken; the (mirtakrha) corpse lies in the courtyard, at the (bare) door.
50P6: Maie = O mother! Mar = death. Mahal = wife. Dar-bare = at the threshold.
(Seeing it again and again) that wife sits weeping at the threshold (and says:) "O mother! (Seeing) this death, my mind has lost its balance."
The widow cries out at the door, "The light of my mind has gone out, O my mother, with his death."
The dead man's wife cries at the door: "with his death, O mother, my intellect is deadened".
"O (maie) friend! By his death my awareness has died" — that is, my mind is not in its place. In this way the (mahal) wife wept (darbare) inside the doorway, or at the door outside.
M510: O soul-brides of the Prabhu, the Husband! Praise the true Prabhu (and so make your life fruitful)! ||5||
So cry out, O soul-brides of the Husband Lord, and dwell on the Glorious Praises of the True Lord. ||5||
O the Husband's brides, by remembering the True Lord's praise, shed you the tears of His love.
Guru ji says: O (mahelio) wives who are seekers! Weep while dwelling on the virtues of the true Husband. ||5||
MQ76: Jal = with water. Mal = rubbing. Jani = by the dear relatives. Kaparh = with cloth. Pat = with silk. Ambare = ambar, with cloth.
Relatives bathe (the body of the one who has died), rubbing it with water, and (wrap it) in silk (and other) cloth.
Her loved one is cleansed, bathed in water, and dressed in silken robes.
The dear one is cleansed and bathed with water and is robed in good many silk clothes.
(Jani) the dear body — or the loved ones — rubbed it with water and bathed it; then with cloths and (pat) a board they made a (ambare) bier.
53CA: Vaje vaje = the words began to be spoken. Sachi bani = the ever-abiding word, "Ram's Name is true." Panch = the relatives (mother, father, brother, wife, son). Mue = became like the dead with grief. Man mare = man mar, crushing the mind, swallowing grief.
(To carry it to the cremation ground) the words "Ram's Name is true" begin, and the close relatives become like the dead with grief.
The musicians play, and the Bani of the True Lord's Words are sung; the five relatives feel as if they too are dead, so deadened are their minds.
The bands play to the chanting of the True words. With numbed mind, the five kindreds feel like the dead.

The instruments of the true word, "Ram's Name is true", were played; the five organs of knowledge went slack, and the thoughts of the mind died too. Or: (man mare) with the soul's death, these five relatives — mother, father, wife, son and brother — died; that is, became grief-stricken.
BZPD: (His wife weeps and says:) "With my companion's death I too have become like one dead; now a curse on my living in the world."
"Separation from my beloved is like death to me!" cries the widow. "My life in this world is cursed and worthless!"
Cries the wife, "separation of my beloved is death for me. Accursed is now my life in this world".
Then the wife says: "With the death of my (jani) beloved, my own death has come; now a curse on my life in the world."
PHSW: But whoever dies while living — that is, gives up attachment — receives honour (in Parmatma's presence). ||6||
But she alone is approved, who dies, while yet still alive; she lives for the sake of the Love of her Beloved. ||6||
She, who, while alive, dies for the sake of the love of her true spouse, is deemed to live.
But true dying happens when one dies while living — that is, in spirit — through love of the true Husband. ||6||
4QHQ: Jhooth = by false attachment. Muthi = robbed.
O soul-brides! You have come into the world only to suffer, because in the world attachment to Maya has cheated you.
So cry out in mourning, you who have come to mourn; this world is false and fraudulent.
Wail you, O women, who have come to wail, but false is the bewailing of the defrauded world.
At such a time Guru ji says: you who have come to weep, (muthi) cheated in the false world — go on weeping.
